newsitem.title: UK: Bass leads charge in brewing sector.
newsitem.headline: Bass leads charge in brewing sector.

text.p: Shares in brewer to leisure group Bass Plc rose 23-1/2p to 767p in early trade on Thursday, after investors and industry took the view Gordon Brown's budget measures were unlikely to curb consumer spending.
"The sector was being held back by budget fears and the worst hasn't happened, which was a much tougher squeeze on the consumer," said Colin Humphreys, drinks analyst at Panmure Gordon.
Shares in Whitbread Plc, owners of Marriott Hotels, pub restaurant chain Brewers Fayre, and French bistro-style Cafe Rouge and Cafe Dome saw its shares surge 13-1/2p to 773p.
Stock in Britain's largest brewer Scottish and Newcastle Plc, owners of holiday camps Center Parcs, gained 13-1/2p to 666-1/2p.

Brown said in his budget statement yesterday that consumer spending should rise by 4.5 percent this year and 4.0 percent in 1998. "With the prospect of further windfalls from building societies, consumer spending is likely to remain strong," he said.
